clue.text: Seek information at pole about husky

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole string built from the other pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to trawl is to search widely for information, as through records
S is the abbreviation for the South Pole

explanation.surface: An explorer at the pole asks questions about a sled dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the whole of TRAWL + AT + S, so TRAWLATS read backwards gives the answer. 'husky' looks like the dog but is the adjective for strong and sturdy.
explanation.definitionFit: Husky can mean sturdy and strongly built, which is the sense of a dependable, robust person.

clue.text: A back seat

parts.note: read not as the rear seat of a car but as a seat placed on a back, such as a horse's

explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits on a horse's back on this leather seat, so it is literally a seat on a back.

clue.text: Beast causing the French bird to take flight

indicators.note: in a down clue taking flight means rising up the grid, so the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for 'the'
a mina, also spelt myna or mynah, is a talking bird of the starling family

explanation.surface: A creature frightens off a French bird so that it flies away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take flight' turns LA + MINA upwards, giving LAMINA read backwards. 'Beast' is the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any creature other than a human, the general sense of a living creature such as a dog or lion.

clue.text: Monitor hunter, possibly with hound

parts.note: a hunter is a pocket timepiece with a hinged cover, so it is an example of a timepiece
a hound is a dog

explanation.surface: Someone on a shoot keeps an eye on a huntsman and his hound.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter is a pocket timepiece with a metal lid; 'possibly' marks it as one example of the kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulatory body that keeps an eye on an industry is a guardian or overseer, which is what a monitor does.

clue.text: For him the alternative is to go up by railway

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading upwards, so the little word for an alternative is turned round

parts.note: or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A man whose other option is to travel north by train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go up' turns OR into RO, and 'by' places RY beside it. 'him' stands for a man's name, a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to an unnamed man, and this is a common male first name, so any man so called fits.

clue.text: Let free, snake heads for somewhere to stay by the water

definitions.text: somewhere to stay by the water

indicators.note: heads means goes in front, so the snake comes before the next piece

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

indicators.note: set free, the letters of the word let are loosed into a new order

explanation.surface: A snake let loose makes for a waterside lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges LET to TEL, and 'heads' puts BOA at the front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatel is a waterside hotel offering moorings for guests who arrive by boat.

clue.text: Bird seen by very large quarry

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, the clothing label for very large
quarry is the animal hunted, its prey

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted near a huge stone pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarry' suggests a stone pit but means the hunted animal; 'seen by' just places the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large fish-eating hawk, also called the fish hawk, so it is a type of raptor.

clue.text: A tin hat I adapted for someone on tropic island

indicators.note: adapted means altered into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone modifies a tin hat to wear on a tropical island.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Pacific island of the Society group, in French Polynesia, is so called.

clue.text: Rarely, it turns out, as well read

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters of the two words are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: It emerges that someone is seldom well read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' looks like part of 'it turns out', but it is fodder: RARELY + IT rearranged by 'turns out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well read knows books thoroughly, which describes a bookish, cultured person.

clue.text: Not on a set course, at sea?

definitions.text: Not on a set course, at sea?

parts.words: Not on a set course, at sea?
parts.note: describes boats that float with the current rather than steering, and also aimless people who wander through life

explanation.definitionFit: Fishing boats that float with their nets are so called, and so are aimless wanderers without a fixed path.

clue.text: Outcome of anti-aircraft fire?

definitions.meaning: humorously read as a shot aimed upward into the sky

explanation.definitionFit: The final result of events is the outcome, while guns firing into the sky literally shoot skywards.

clue.text: They take pot-shots — monarchs stalk birds

indicators.note: to stalk is to follow behind, so the monarchs come after the birds

parts.note: snipe are wading birds; the plural is the same as the singular
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen, so two of them make RS

explanation.surface: Kings and queens creep up on some game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stalk' means follow, putting RS after SNIPE. R, for rex or regina, is a standard abbreviation for a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden marksmen fire at targets from cover, the sense of taking pot-shots at people.

clue.text: See one article then another to despise

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
a is the indefinite article
the is the other article, the definite one

explanation.surface: Someone looks at one article and then another, coming to scorn them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' is grammar, not a newspaper piece: A is the indefinite article, and 'another' gives THE, the definite one.
explanation.definitionFit: To despise is to detest or hate intensely, the same strong dislike.

clue.text: He discovers — in an opening — gold!

parts.note: a vent is an opening that lets air or gas escape
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A prospector cries out on finding gold in a gap in the rock.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry, a standard crossword convention. 'He discovers' stands for a person who comes up with new devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who devises a new machine or process is said to discover or create it.

clue.text: Used to reduce swelling number of arctic wolves?

definitions.meaning: a bag of frozen cubes held against a bruise or sprain
humorously, a group of wolves in a frozen land

explanation.definitionFit: A cold compress of frozen material soothes injuries, and a group of polar wolves would be a frozen band.

clue.text: Used by surgeon on muscle as an afterthought?

parts.note: muscle means strength or force
PS, postscript, is the afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: A surgeon uses muscle, almost as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: PS is the postscript tacked onto a letter, the standard crossword 'afterthought'.
explanation.definitionFit: These pincers are a gripping instrument used in operations and childbirth.

clue.text: Den left to ventilate

parts.note: to air a room is to ventilate it

explanation.surface: A den has been left open so it can get some fresh breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's den is its home or hiding place.

clue.text: Hot lamb left over? Put it under wraps

indicators.note: over suggests the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Some leftover roast lamb, still hot, is covered up and put away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges HOT LAMB, and L for 'left' goes at the end. 'left over' looks like one phrase about leftovers but splits into two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a project or put a ship into storage is to set it aside under protective covers.

clue.text: Ringing, get information held by lodge

indicators.note: held by means the information is kept inside the word for lodge

parts.note: to lodge something is to plant or fix it firmly
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone gets information from a Masonic lodge on the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lodge' is the verb, to fix firmly, not a club building. GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A plangent sound is loud, resonant and often mournful, like a bell's reverberation.

clue.text: Doctor in case journalist harassed

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
lest means for fear that, in case
ED, editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A doctor in a legal case is pestered by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case' looks like a legal case but is LEST, meaning for fear that.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestered or attacked, the sense of being troubled or bothered persistently.

clue.text: Birds observed in slow motion

indicators.note: motion means the letters of the word slow are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Birds watched as a replay runs at reduced speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motion' rearranges SLOW. 'slow motion' looks like a single phrase about film replays.
explanation.definitionFit: These nocturnal raptors with large eyes are a family of hunting birds.

clue.text: Robin's killer as an afterthought returns the weapon

indicators.note: returns means the abbreviation for an afterthought comes back the other way

parts.note: PS, postscript, is the afterthought added to a letter
an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

explanation.surface: Robin's murderer, almost as an afterthought, gives back the weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme 'Who Killed Cock Robin?' the culprit says it was done 'with my bow and arrow'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old nursery rhyme the small brown bird confesses to shooting Cock Robin.

clue.text: To be thus blunt can be stupid

definitions.meaning: not sharp or pointed, as an angle wider than ninety degrees

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a rounded, not pointed, shape and also a slow-witted person who misses the point.

clue.text: Exercise, carrying breathing equipment, then dive

indicators.note: carrying means the letters for exercise hold the breathing organ inside them

parts.note: PE, physical education, is exercise
a lung is the body's breathing organ

explanation.surface: After exercise with scuba gear, someone dives in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathing equipment' suggests scuba gear but is the body's own LUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to dive or jump headlong into water.

clue.text: The deep issue — spring, perhaps

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: Water rises from the ocean depths like a spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like a water source but is the time of year; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring is one of the four quarters of the year, an example of a time of year.

clue.text: Show reluctance to suspend the footballer

parts.note: to suspend is to hang
a back is a defensive footballer

explanation.surface: Fans are hesitant to ban the defender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspend' looks like a disciplinary ban, but it is simply to hang.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate or hold off from going forward is to be reluctant.

clue.text: I'll see if it changes him

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the phrase are altered into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone vows to check whether a man has altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges I'LL SEE. 'him' stands for a man's name, a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to an unnamed man, and this is a male first name, so any man so called fits.

clue.text: Throw the ball in the basin

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to deliver the ball to the batsman

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a delivery to the batsman is made this way, and a deep round dish has the same name.

clue.text: Approach a meeting-place

parts.note: a venue is a place where people meet for an event

explanation.surface: Someone makes an approach to a meeting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' is a noun: a drive or tree-lined road leading to a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-lined drive up to a country house is called its approach.

clue.text: A number of melodies reputedly making millions

indicators.note: reputedly means as said or reported, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: four is a number, and tunes are melodies, giving four tunes

explanation.surface: Some songs, it is said, earn their writers vast sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reputedly' signals that 'four tunes' is heard aloud; the phrase 'four tunes' sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Large sums of money, as in making a fortune, are vast wealth.

clue.text: Form of transport for the young?

definitions.meaning: a curtained couch carried on poles by bearers
a set of newborn animals, such as puppies, born together

explanation.definitionFit: A curtained couch carried by bearers was an old way to travel, and newborn puppies or kittens form a brood.

clue.text: Chum casually hijacking student, gone off to club

indicators.note: hijacking means the chum takes the student inside

parts.note: bud is a casual, informal word for a chum or buddy
L, learner, is the abbreviation for a student

indicators.note: off means the letters of gone have gone bad and are scrambled

explanation.surface: A mate grabs a student and goes off to a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges GONE to GEON. 'club' looks like a nightclub but is the verb to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To club someone is to beat them with a heavy stick, which is what a cudgel does.
